title: Google Plans to End All Pixel Manufacturing in China by 2027
excerpt: The tech giant is moving both development and production of its flagship smartphones to Vietnam, marking a near-total exit from Chinese manufacturing amid tariff pressures.
body:
• Google plans to stop making all Pixel products in China by 2027, moving development and production to Vietnam
  • The shift includes new product introduction (NPI) — the critical engineering phase that had remained in China even after assembly moved out
  • Flagship Pixel, Pixel Pro, and Pixel Fold lines will all move, while budget A-Series phones remain in China for now
  • The decision is driven by rising tariffs, geopolitical tensions, and a broader tech industry exodus from Chinese manufacturing

Google is planning to fully withdraw Pixel smartphone manufacturing from China by 2027, Nikkei Asia reported, in what would mark the most comprehensive production shift by a major American tech company away from the world's largest electronics manufacturing hub.

Beyond Assembly: Moving the Engineering

The move goes significantly further than relocating assembly lines. Google will shift new product introductions — the critical development, verification, and fine-tuning phase where hundreds of engineers prepare a new device for mass production — from China to Vietnam for all flagship Pixel models, according to the Nikkei report.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Jonm5qRkoMo

NPI has traditionally been the last phase companies move out of China because it requires deep supplier relationships, specialized equipment, and experienced engineering talent. Until now, even as Google shifted final assembly to Vietnam starting in 2022, this critical pre-production work continued at Chinese facilities.

"If NPI fails, then it means there will be no new product for the year. Building new phones from scratch in Vietnam should be achievable since Google already carries out some verification processes there."

— Source familiar with Google's plans, via Nikkei Asia

Scope of the Shift

The relocation covers Google's entire premium lineup: the standard Pixel, Pixel Pro, and Pixel Fold. Development of the budget-oriented Pixel A-Series will remain in China "for now," the report noted, suggesting even that line could eventually follow.

Google has been gradually building its Vietnamese manufacturing footprint since 2019, when it began converting a former Nokia factory in Bac Ninh province — the same region where Samsung built its smartphone supply chain. Some Pixel production already takes place in Vietnam and India, but this latest plan would make Vietnam the primary global hub for Pixel hardware development.

Tariffs and Geopolitics

The acceleration is driven by a convergence of factors. U.S. tariffs on Chinese-made electronics have steadily increased under both the Trump and Biden administrations, eating into margins for companies that manufacture in China and sell primarily in the United States. Google sold roughly 70% of its Pixel phones in the U.S. market, making it particularly exposed to these duties.

Rising Chinese labor costs and supply chain disruption risks have compounded the financial pressure. Google is not alone in this calculus — Dell, HP, Microsoft, and Amazon have all announced plans to shift portions of their hardware production out of China, according to previous Nikkei reporting.

India's Role in the Supply Chain

While Vietnam is the primary destination for Pixel production, Google has also expanded manufacturing in India for certain models. India's growing electronics manufacturing ecosystem, bolstered by government incentives under the Production Linked Incentive scheme, has attracted major smartphone makers including Apple, Samsung, and Xiaomi. Google's presence in Indian manufacturing could expand further as the company diversifies its supply chain across Southeast and South Asia.

What's Next

The transition is expected to begin with the Pixel 11 series this year, with a complete exit from Chinese manufacturing targeted for 2027. Apple, by contrast, continues to conduct NPIs in both China and other regions, maintaining a dual-track approach that Google appears to be moving beyond. The shift will be closely watched as a bellwether for whether other consumer electronics companies follow suit with full manufacturing exits from China.
